setting: First half: Start with exact incoming empty meadow, right-side pale wall and willow, all geometry unchanged. Giraffe must be located farther back beyond the existing wall return so its entire projected silhouette is truly hidden at frame0, not directly behind a low wall at family distance. Position is a creative staging condition requiring a coherent keyframe; no new taller wall may grow between frames. Second half: Same giraffe meadow rail and feeding branch; tall opaque pale divider close to camera separates adjoining tiger bay. Tiger not visible in this segment.
lighting: Soft warm morning daylight; broad key from upper screen-left, gentle cream bounce fill, no hard rim or colored neon light. Stable white balance and exposure on peach skin and muted rose/dusty-teal/sage clothes; pale sky and restrained greens. Same light direction across cuts.
camera: First half: Continue gentle tracking on original path-left side; a small lateral-left translation changes sightline around the existing wall left edge to reveal the more distant giraffe. Keep family visible and camera height/exposure stable; no180-degree orbit, sudden wall replacement, fast zoom or whole-frame wipe. Second half: Small upward tilt only to establish tall neck; keep parents and toddler in frame. Settle before words finish, then track one step along same side. End with pale rock divider entering far right. Preserve the path-left camera side. Face visibility comes from a modest LEFT head turn toward mother, not from turning the torso away from the travel axis; never force full frontal face.
action: First half: Carry exact incoming walking pose, empty meadow and fixed wall. Finish one small step and settle. Continuous small path-left camera translation reveals a giraffe positioned farther behind wall return, emerging around wall left edge before original line1.00; reveal must be geometrically plausible. If this cannot fit one second, reject/revise staging keyframe before generation rather than make animal pop or alter dialogue. Toddler notices giraffe, points RIGHT/up, then gives small LEFT head glance toward mother for exact line. Feet/torso keep path axis. After speech gaze returns to giraffe as its head inclines. Bird remains out of frame; no reverse pan to perch. Second half: Start from inclined giraffe head. Giraffe slowly extends toward leaves during the exact guided line; tiny upward tilt keeps all family visible, then settles. After tall-giraffe line, lower pointing hand and take at most one small step along rail as camera tracks a short distance. A nearby tall pale divider wall progressively occludes the entire giraffe including neck and feet by used119. Wall covers only habitat sightline; family remains continuously visible. Tiger is still hidden beyond wall return, no tiger appearance here. Speech mouth motion follows only the exact guide. Torso and feet keep path direction; a small LEFT head turn addresses mother while the right pointing arm may still indicate the animal. Parents answer with one silent nod or smile. No swing between multiple addressees. During exact line maintain modest LEFT profile toward mother while pointing RIGHT/up; gaze may return to giraffe after words. Do not demand simultaneous eye contact with mother and giraffe.
music: Gentle cheerful original pentatonic plucked/marimba-style instrumental, no lyrics, quiet underneath canonical Alice, duck smoothly during all words, stable modest level through transitions.
